limitations: Trusted entry execution, not a sandbox or arbitrary uploaded-code service.
Returns and real call/argument ancestry are observations, not complete dynamic dataflow.

Observed prefix hashes complete portable return values and explicit opaque type/location markers; it is not a serialization of opaque heap state. Paired runs copy the actual live state by os.fork and must match the parent baseline.
Actual argument previews are captured only at the chosen split; compact container hashes are candidate-ranking hints, not causality or replay guards.
Canonical returns above 2 KiB are completely hashed for the prefix but not retained as intervention candidates; output selection never authorizes completed-artifact replacement.
Candidate priority is not inferred dataflow; only selected-output changes confirmed by guarded fresh replay establish influence on this run.
Temporary return replacement is a counterfactual experiment, not a source-level repair.
Recorded call ancestry and bounded argument previews are not complete causal dataflow.

Recorded, unauthenticated receipts and local-byte checks do not establish a causal theorem or source repair. Native fork does not roll back external state. Fresh replay remains local to the pinned source, engine and interpreter environment.
